chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no one except that he has vigour and slackening. So whoever's slackening leads him to the sunnah has been guided, and whoever's slackening leads him to an innovation has deviated.

key_terms.بِدْعَةٍ: bid'a — a blameworthy religious innovation introduced without prophetic sanction, a cause of deviation
key_terms.سُنَّةٍ: sunnah — the established prophetic tradition as the normative guide for religious practice
key_terms.شِرَّةٌ: vigour, zeal — intense initial religious enthusiasm or spiritual energy
key_terms.فَتْرَةٌ: slackening, lull — a natural period of reduced religious motivation or activity

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir (AS) teach about the spiritual consequences of one's period of slackening in devotion leading toward either the sunnah or bid'a?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) acknowledges a universal feature of human religious life: every person naturally alternates between periods of intense zeal (shirra) and periods of laxity (fatra). The decisive spiritual criterion is not whether one experiences laxity, but where one turns during those periods — adherence to the sunnah brings guidance, while drifting toward bid'a (blameworthy innovation) leads to misguidance and deviation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is no one except there is for him vigour and calmness. So the one who was such that his calmness leads him to a Sunnah, so he has been guided, and the one who was such that his calmness leads him to an innovation, so he has deviated’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following. “

There is no one without excitement and calmness. Whoever’s calmness would lead him towards the Sunnah, noble traditions of the holy prophet (s.a.), he is rightly guided but if it would lead him towards innovations then he has gone astray.”
